channel.title: Kompas — News
channel.description: Key news on repression in Russia and against those who left: political prisoners, verdicts, new designations. Every item links to its source. Updated morning and evening.

item.title: Historian Yury Dmitriev taken to hospital from penal colony with suspected stroke
item.description: According to the rights project ZPCh, the founder of the Sandarmokh memorial, serving 15 years, was urgently moved from penal colony No. 18 in Mordovia to a prison medical facility. A lawyer will try to visit him on 26 September. — Mediazona

item.title: Belarus: 27-year-old aviator sentenced to 13 years for “treason”
item.description: According to the Viasna human rights centre, Minsk City Court gave Sviatoslau Padvashetski 13 years in an enhanced-security colony on treason and drug charges. The trial was held behind closed doors. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: Minsk bank employee who called Russian troops occupiers convicted
item.description: According to Nasha Niva, a 50-year-old MTBank employee was convicted by Minsk City Court of inciting hatred over social media posts criticising Russia’s aggression. His sentence is unknown; he is in custody. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: First known jail term in Yekaterinburg over “Ural Republic” flag
item.description: A court jailed the admin of the “Urals Chat” Telegram group for 10 days over two posts showing the flag of a movement the FSB listed as terrorist in 2025. It is the first known such case, 7x7 reports. — 7x7

item.title: Azerbaijan: theologian jailed for 30 days after criticising school hijab restrictions
item.description: Abgul Suleymanov’s family link his administrative detention to his posts against restrictions on schoolgirls wearing the hijab. Police and the court gave no public reason, JAMnews reports, citing Meydan TV. — JAMnews

item.title: Political scientist Alexander Kynev remanded in custody on drug charges
item.description: A Moscow court sent the elections expert, already labelled a “foreign agent”, to pre-trial detention on a large-scale drug dealing charge carrying up to 20 years. He denies it. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: St Petersburg lawyer Nurdi Shamaev jailed over a four-year-old comment
item.description: A district court remanded the lawyer in custody on charges of “justifying terrorism” over a social media post. — Mediazona

item.title: “Khodorkovsky LIVE” designated a “foreign agent”
item.description: The Justice Ministry added the news YouTube channel, which has more than 3 million subscribers, to its register of “foreign agents”. — Mediazona

item.title: YouTuber “Ded Arkhimed” arrested in absentia over “fakes” and foreign-agent rules
item.description: A court in Ivanovo ordered the arrest in absentia of the 53-year-old blogger on charges of spreading army “fakes” and evading “foreign agent” obligations. — Mediazona

item.title: Four residents of occupied Melitopol sentenced to 17 to 28 years
item.description: The Southern District Military Court convicted them of plotting attacks on Russian-installed officials. — Mediazona

item.title: Two Tula men, detained as teenagers, jailed for 6 and 7 years over railway arson
item.description: The Tula regional court sentenced them for setting fire to a trackside equipment cabinet. — Mediazona

item.title: Border officers extract phone data via Bluetooth
item.description: Equipment used at Russian border checks can pull call history and contact lists from travellers’ phones over Bluetooth. — Mediazona

item.title: Jailed lawyer Roman Melnichenko is losing his sight
item.description: The imprisoned lawyer and former Volgograd university lecturer has suffered a sharp decline in vision, and doctors refuse to treat him, OVD-Info reports. — OVD-Info

item.title: Jailed Crimean Tatar with liver cancer in critical condition
item.description: Human rights defenders say the 58-year-old political prisoner is in a critical state in a prison hospital in the Arkhangelsk region. — Mediazona

item.title: US court grants bail to Russian asylum seeker
item.description: Artyom Kosolapov had been held in immigration detention in Arkansas since late August. Bail was set at $15,000; he still faces possible deportation. — The Insider

item.title: Yekaterinburg pensioner given 240 hours’ community service for donations to a Ukrainian church
item.description: Nadezhda Esina, 67, was convicted over donations to the “Vozrozhdenie” church. — Mediazona

item.title: Two teenagers from Angarsk get almost 9 and 10 years for trying to set fire to military vehicles
item.description: A military court convicted a 15-year-old and a 17-year-old on terrorism and treason charges for throwing Molotov cocktails at a military unit; the vehicles were not damaged. — Mediazona

item.title: Two St Petersburg residents sentenced to 13 years for treason
item.description: The St Petersburg City Court gave Oksana Ronzhes and Artyom Sakharov 13 years each: they were accused of filming power lines and the area near a military airfield on the orders of Ukraine's GUR. — Mediazona

item.title: Former CEO of the Domovyonok service Nikita Zhilin put on wanted list over donations to FBK
item.description: The Interior Ministry is seeking Zhilin, who lives abroad, in a case of financing FBK. By Mediazona's count, 167 sentences have already been handed down in such cases. — Mediazona

item.title: 7x7 journalist Marina Skorikova put on federal wanted list
item.description: A case for calls to act against state security has been opened against the journalist, who was designated a "foreign agent" in spring 2026. — Mediazona

item.title: Daughter of Novosibirsk man says FSB officers tortured her father
item.description: According to Tonya Egorova, her father was detained on 15 September and tortured to make him confess to setting fire to a cell tower. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: Defendants in Rostov car arson case tell court of beatings and questioning without a lawyer
item.description: Defendants in the case of a burnt car belonging to an officer's wife told the court they were beaten during arrest and questioned without a defence lawyer. — Mediazona

item.title: Rosfinmonitoring list includes 518 teenagers, the youngest aged 14
item.description: Since June the number of minors on the list of "terrorists and extremists" has grown by 53. The youngest person on it was born in 2012. — The Insider

item.title: FBK staffer Yulia Emelyanova faces extradition as Kazakhstan denies her asylum
item.description: Kazakhstan has finally refused asylum to the Navalny team member, and she may now be handed over to Russia. — Radio Liberty

item.title: Finland grants asylum to anti-war Russians the Belovs, who faced deportation
item.description: Olga and Nikita Belov, whom the authorities wanted to deport to Russia in the spring, have been granted asylum in Finland. — Meduza

item.title: Tyumen man sentenced to 8 years for Telegram Stars worth 293 roubles
item.description: A military court convicted 57-year-old Mikhail Antonovich of "financing terrorism": he left paid reactions in the channels of Naki, Nevzorov and Shpak. — OVD-Info

item.title: Komsomolsk-on-Amur man sentenced to 15 years for lift graffiti and comments about the Legion
item.description: A military court gave him 15 years in a strict-regime colony for graffiti in a lift and comments supporting the Freedom of Russia Legion, under treason and justifying-terrorism charges. — Mediazona

item.title: Yury Dud added to Rosfinmonitoring's list of "terrorists and extremists"
item.description: The journalist has been added to the list, so his bank transactions in Russia will be blocked. — OVD-Info

item.title: TV Rain host Mikhail Fishman goes on trial in absentia for involvement in an "undesirable organisation"
item.description: Moscow's Simonovsky court is hearing the case under Article 284.1 of the Criminal Code. The defence says Fishman is being prosecuted for his journalism. — Mediazona

item.title: Prosecutor General's Office declares a German foundation, Crimea's Almenda centre and "Friends of Falun Gong" "undesirable"
item.description: The list now includes a German foundation supporting ethnic Germans, the Ukrainian civic education centre Almenda and a British organisation. — The Insider

item.title: New case over calls to terrorism opened against blogger Alexander Shpak
item.description: The case is based on a 2024 video. Shpak, previously sentenced in absentia to 8 years over "fakes", will be charged in absentia. — OVD-Info

item.title: Memorial asks Durov to make paid Telegram reactions anonymous
item.description: The Memorial Political Prisoners Support project says the public list of Stars senders is a vulnerability that security forces use to open terrorism financing cases. — OVD-Info

item.title: Barents Observer journalist Denis Zagore charged and put on wanted list
item.description: The Murmansk "foreign agent" journalist is accused of breaking the "foreign agent" rules and taking part in an "undesirable" organisation. — OVD-Info

item.title: Muscovite detained at a polling station says he was tortured with a stun gun
item.description: Alexander Pavlov says that after he tried to photograph the election commission's notice board, police beat him and shocked him more than 20 times. — OVD-Info

item.title: Political prisoner and saxophonist Andrei Shabanov asks to be included in a prisoner swap
item.description: The musician, who has a disability and was convicted over posts criticising the Kremlin, described pressure in the penal colony and asked to be put on the exchange lists. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: Justice Ministry designates film director Andrei Zvyagintsev a "foreign agent"
item.description: The ministry said the director had worked with "foreign agents" and "undesirable" organisations. Several other people were added to the list at the same time. — OVD-Info

item.title: Interior Ministry puts Meduza journalist Vladislav Gorin on wanted list
item.description: The journalist, whose outlet is designated "undesirable", has been added to the wanted database. — OVD-Info

item.title: Rybinsk artist sentenced to eight years for money transfers to Vyacheslav Maltsev
item.description: The court ruled that the transfers to the blogger amounted to financing extremism. — OVD-Info

item.title: Zhanna Nemtsova put on international wanted list
item.description: The journalist and daughter of Boris Nemtsov has been put on the international wanted list in a criminal case. — OVD-Info
